findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including the seed object with vendor data) are not encrypted at rest by default.

findings.issue_category: missing access control / no ACL or public access block
findings.description: No 'acl' attribute is set and no public-access-block configuration is present, leaving the bucket to potentially default to unintended access settings and lacking explicit private access enforcement.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial ledger export data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined despite storing model artifacts, leaving them unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving operational runbook data unencrypted at rest.

The acl attribute is set to the malformed/non-standard value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' instead of a valid canned ACL such as 'log-delivery-write-access' or 'private'. This is likely a misconfiguration that could result in Terraform failing or defaulting to an unintended, more permissive ACL, risking exposure of sensitive audit trail data.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data uploaded to unencrypted bucket
findings.description: This object (vendor-roster.xlsx, likely containing sensitive vendor data) is uploaded to aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which has no encryption configuration and no explicit private ACL, increasing risk of unauthorized access or unencrypted storage of sensitive data.
